These two asshats come into the library (and I do mean asshats - or maybe I mean ass hats? - literally, by the way . . . you'll see) wearing those bright red with white print Make America Great Again hats (see?) the other day.

It presents a bit of a quandary for me as library staff because wearing offensive clothing in the library isn't cool, yo. For example, if someone comes in wearing a tee reading "Hitler Rulez" on one side and "Death2NonWhites" on the other? We're kicking them out until they wear more appropriate clothing.

Library pro-tip: If you're making patrons uneasy because you're calling for their genocide, well, that tends to go against library policy.

On the other hand, simply because a patron is offended doesn't mean we're taking action.

If, for instance, you're using the patron computers and occasionally swearing under your breath because working with Microsoft Word is frustrating you to no end, and another patron, also at the patron computers, takes offense at such language and brings it to the attention of staff? We're not gonna do much about it. Cursing quietly at Microsoft is not against library policy. We will ask the offended patron if they want to move to another computer so they're out of aural range, but that's about it.

Unfortunately, in the real life example of the issue above, the offended patron thought they shouldn't have to move and asked to speak to the director. The library director came, listened to them, then asked if they wanted to move. The patron repeated their desire to not move, then, eventually, after finishing their work, did decide to move . . . completely outside the library . . . for, based on the last couple months they haven't been in, good.

But back to the asshats ass hats.

So as I see them approaching me, I have to make a split-second decision: Do I kick them out because of their blatant support of an utterly offensive person whose very existence harms all of humanity?

Probably not.

But it's sorely tempting.

What I do do is help them with their tech issue and get a "See? I told you he'd help us," from one of the couple grinning at the other of the couple just before they leave, which, if I'm honest, makes me feel slightly slimy personally and slightly fulfilled professionally.

P.S. - Interestingly enough, when I spellchecked this little diddy, "Death2NonWhites" did not come up as a problem, meaning, I guess, that "Death2NonWhites" is already in the LibreOffice dictionary?

P.P.S - LibreOffice did want to correct "diddy."

P.P.P.S. - Diddy does not seem to mean what I thought it meant.

P.P.P.P.S. - Ah, what I actually meant was "ditty," but it turns out I was using that incorrectly, as well.

It's been nearly a quarter century since i owned the bakiwop.com domain. Tonight? Tonight I couldn't fall asleep so I went downstairs, fired up the pc, and, for some reason, checked to see if it was available (I'd checked on and off over the years to no avail, natch) . . . and there it was, just waiting for me, looking all pretty and shiny on the domain registrar shelf. How cool is that?
